messages: lina: Quick design huddle: we're debating required field signposting and error surfacing for the new Dashboard form. Two options: 1) persistent required label ("Required" text on all labels) + inline errors only, or 2) minimal labels (asterisk) + top error summary on submit. Which is better for discoverability and a11y? marc: My vote0is for persistent "Required" text. Asterisks are ambiguous and teams keep forgetting to add explanatory legend. Helps when fields are complex (e.g., conditional sections). devon: Implementation trade: persistent labels increase vertical density. For long forms it can feel noisy. We could collapse the label into a secondary line for compact mode. Also, summary on submit surfaces all issues at once which some users like. anika: Accessibility: a visible "Required" token that is also exposed to screen readers (e.g., Required) is ideal. Error summary must be role=\"alert\" and focus should move to it on submit failure. Links in summary should programmatically focus the corresponding input. lina: Good point about density. What if we combine: show inline minimal markers (bold label + subtle "Required" for first N fields or above-the-fold fields), and a compact error summary that only appears after failed submit? Inline errors appear after blur. marc: That composition sounds reasonable. Also, copy matters: inline "Required" vs "Please add a value" vs "Missing". Short, action-oriented messages are better inline. Summary can contain fuller guidance like "Email: used to send invoices". devon: Dev note: if inline shows on blur and summary on submit, we need to ensure validators are consistent and not duplicating messages. We should centralize messages in the validation layer (single source of truth) so the summary and inline pull the same copy. anika: Don't forget keyboard-only flows: when a user tabs into the first invalid link in the summary, the input should receive focus and the screen reader should announce the inline message. Use aria-describedby linking to the inline message id. lina: Also want to handle destructive confirmations in the same doc: proposal0— light deletes = confirm modal with plain message + undo toast; dangerous deletes = typed-confirm with the resource name; multi-resource deletes = batch modal with clear counts and a checkbox to acknowledge. marc: For typed-confirm, prefer resource-name pattern over static words. It's less error-prone and communicates context. Eg: "Type project-name to confirm deletion". Include copy that explains rollback options (if any). anika: Accessibility for typed-confirm: label is explicit, and we must ensure error states announce when input doesn't match. If there's a cooldown, visually show a timer AND announce remaining time with aria-live polite. devon: From a platform perspective, typed-confirm needs rate-limiting and audit logging. Also add a small client-side fuzzy-match tolerance? Not a fan; keep exact match to avoid mistakes. lina: Finalize defaults: inline-on-blur for fields, compact summary on submit if >1 error, persistent "Required" for top-of-form fields only (configurable), typed confirms for high-risk deletes. I'll draft the spec and a short copy matrix. marc: Can you include examples for mobile/compact layouts? The vertical space issue is worse on mobile. lina: Yep. I'll add mobile guidelines and a density toggle for power users. uxbot: Logged decisions: inline validation on blur, top summary on failed submit when >1 error, persistent required label for primary fields, typed confirm for org-level deletes. Spec PR requested. anika: I'll review the PR for a11y. Also adding a checklist: aria-required, aria-invalid, error-summary role=alert, focus management, aria-describedby linking. devon: I'll scope the validator changes and ensure message strings are centralized. lina: Thanks all 609 I'll post a draft spec by Friday.
